To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Breast tissue-specific methylation profiles can be generated by comparing purified normal breast epithelila to other normal epithelial tissue; 2) TRIM29 is a tissue-specific breast gene with a breast specific methylation profile; 3) TRIM29 methylation status in breast cancer is associated with breast cancer subtypes; and 4) TRIM29 expression in breast cancer is inversely correlated with methylation.

breast epithelium has a specific methylation signature, which is altered in cancer.

tissue specific DNA methylation is a key factor in tissue specific carcinogenesis.
breast specific methylation is associated with breast specific cancer and that the epigenetic profile of the normal breast epithelulum can guide the choice of the most suitable therapeutic approach.
